recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not force event: [ null ] into these generated JSON examples unless the work group reopens or revises the current FHIR-32806 JSON null-array guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-24079 was a Published FHIR-core change request with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification for ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition generated JSON examples. The reporter noted timingTiming._event primitive extensions without a parallel timingTiming.event array containing null, and the final resolution asked to clarify JSON primitive array handling as two equal length arrays and correct the generated examples to include event: [ null ].
initial_application: No prior FHIR-24079-tagged source commit or combined-branch audit commit was found. The affected ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition resources are active in source/fhir.ini, but their examples are XML source and the complained-about JSON surface is generated by the build; Jira/Zulip discussion identified the symptom as a serialization/tooling question rather than hand-authored JSON source.
additional_context: FHIR-32806 is a later Published FHIR-I decision for the same JSON primitive array null-handling rule. It resolved that when a JSON element array and its _element array differ in length, implementations SHALL infer null suffixes in the shorter array; current source/json.html also says arrays containing only null elements SHOULD be omitted entirely. This later rule makes a generated timingTiming object with _event and an omitted all-null event array conformant.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Requiring explicit equal-length arrays for all-null primitive values in these generated examples would reverse the later applied FHIR-32806 clarification.
